candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether concentrations are treated as geometric means and in ug/l (or an alternate unit) affects which numeric limit is compared against reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Using half the detection limit as the effluent input changes calculated instream concentrations and limit comparisons; it also classifies below-detection results as usable numeric substitutes rather than missing or no-data states.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating the value as no data excludes it from limit calculations and establishes a documented no-data state rather than a numeric compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Choosing the reported value versus zero changes the effluent concentration used in calculations and whether the case is treated as a valid numeric input or an effectively zero/missing result.
Different readings of the instream waste concentration formula and its inputs (F, Qa, Ca, Qe, Ce) change the derived concentration against which effluent or receiving-water limits are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: F = Fraction of stream allow ed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F is a direct input to Cd; a different F value changes calculated instream concentrations and thus which numeric limit applies or whether a measurement exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow is used as Qa changes Cd and can change the applicable numeric discharge or instream limit for human-health-based criteria.

candidates.exact_span: The follow ing formular convert metals reported in total form to dissolved form if criteria are in dissolved form
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether total-reported metals must be converted to dissolved form determines which criteria form (total vs dissolved) is used for limit comparison.

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selecting TSS from the receiving stream versus effluent for intermittent streams changes the partition coefficient and dissolved-metal criteria used in limit determination.
This conversion from dissolved criteria (Cr) to total criteria (Ct) directly sets the enforceable numeric limit when metals are reported in total form.

The stream dissolved value of 0 for Chromium III yields a zero total-metal criterion under the conversion formula, which changes whether a numeric compliance comparison is applicable versus report-only or non-enforceable treatment.

The hardness-dependent acute cadmium formula and CF1 correction factor determine the applicable acute dissolved limit; different hardness or CF1 interpretation changes the numeric limit used for comparison.

The hardness-dependent chronic cadmium formula and CF2 correction factor determine the applicable chronic dissolved limit; different hardness or CF2 interpretation changes the numeric limit used for comparison.
